decisions.notebook: Rage Powder redirects all opposing single-target moves to user; always target the Rage Powder user directly or use spread moves that avoid ally damage. Never use Earthquake with a non-Flying/non-Levitate ally present—Aegislash takes 2x Ground. Rotom-Heat at -4 SpA deals minimal damage (~20-30) to our high-SpD Aegislash; prioritize KOing support (Sinistcha/Gholdengo) before they heal or redirect. Durable core plan: keep Archaludon healthy with Leftovers, use Aegislash King's Shield only against physical threats, and eliminate Rock-type bench (Tyranitar/Excadrill) before setting up Volcarona Quiver Dance. Focus Sash is unreliable below full HP; avoid relying on it.

decisions.rationale: Rotom's SpA reset to 172 after the switch, so Overheat is a guaranteed KO on Aegislash-Blade from 90% and, unlike Excadrill's High Horsepower, it can't be punished by King's Shield (no Atk drop, no self SpA drop if blocked). Excadrill's High Horsepower into Archaludon (81-138%) either KOs or breaks Sturdy down to ~1 HP, setting up a clean finish next turn, and Rotom is immune to Archaludon's Earthquake retaliation.

decisions.rationale: Aegislash is vulnerable to Rotom Overheat (possible OHKO) and Excadrill physical hits; King's Shield (priority +4) protects it and lowers attackers' Attack. Earthquake is super-effective (2x) on Excadrill and spread-hits, but Rotom-Heat is Levitate-immune; with Aegislash shielded by King's Shield, ally takes no Ground damage. This deals heavy spread damage to Excadrill while keeping our special attacker alive.

decisions.rationale: Rotom Thunderbolt guarantees the KO on Archaludon at 6% (Sturdy irrelevant, no Protect assumed), while Excadrill High Horsepower is a guaranteed KO on Aegislash at 90% even in Shield forme — that wins the game outright since Volcarona/Corviknight are already down.
